channel.title: Hadi Mohammadi — Blog
channel.description: Field notes on building and evaluating production LLM systems, and open guides for people studying AI and data science.

item.title: Ask a model how sure it is
item.description: Three local models answered 1,000 MMLU questions each and rated their own confidence from 0 to 100. Mean stated confidence ran from 88 to 98 while accuracy ran from 62 to 78, and on all three a constant base rate beat the stated number. What the audit looks like, with calikit.

item.title: What a benchmark can actually tell apart
item.description: HumanEval has 164 problems, which means it cannot resolve a gap under 9 points. Of five benchmarks people quote weekly, only MMLU comes within reach of a one-point claim. The floor for each, and the one-minute calculation to run before building an eval.

item.title: How much text a watermark needs before it shows up
item.description: Anthropic began watermarking Claude's output this month. A circulating simulation of a simplified green-list scheme puts detection at a couple of hundred words. The arithmetic holds. Its assumption that every token is a real choice does not, and that moves the number by a factor of six.

item.title: The labels under the benchmark
item.description: An audit of the 211,225 raw crowd ratings behind GoEmotions: 27 of 28 emotions fall below the 0.667 reliability floor, rater quality spans a factor of three, and the dataset has a third of the raters per item the task needs.

item.title: What an LLM judge actually does when you are not looking
item.description: Three local LLM judges graded the same adversarial arithmetic benchmark in both presentation orders. One picked whichever answer came first 91% of the time; another graded effort and scored no better than chance.

item.title: Calling LLMs well
item.description: Structured outputs, retries, streaming, caching and cost control: the unglamorous 80% of production LLM work.

item.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
item.description: Chunking, hybrid search, reranking and query rewriting: RAG treated as an information-retrieval problem, and how it actually fails.

item.title: Agents and MCP
item.description: Tool loops, the Model Context Protocol, planning patterns and agent evaluation, and when a plain workflow beats an agent.

item.title: Fine-tuning and preference optimization
item.description: A decision table for RAG versus prompting versus LoRA versus DPO and GRPO, then the mechanics of each.

item.title: Evaluation and LLM-as-judge
item.description: The five-level eval hierarchy, how to build an LLM judge you can defend, why agreement is the metric behind the metric.

item.title: Serving and inference optimization
item.description: Prefill and decode, vLLM and continuous batching, KV caches, quantization, and the cost arithmetic behind API versus self-host.
